https://telex.hu/gazdasag/2026/09/07/kap.text: Menü Kereső Kapitány István feljelentést tett a Waberer's korábbi MFB-finanszírozásai miatt Gazdaság Barnóczki Brigitta Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „A mai napon feljelentést tettem ismeretlen tettes ellen, a Waberer's korábbi MFB finanszírozásai miatt!” – jelentette be Kapitány István a Facebookon. A gazdasági és energetikai miniszter a videóposztjában azt mondta, a minisztériuma végzi az állami pénzügyi intézmények korábbi finanszírozási döntéseinek átvilágítását, ennek során pedig két olyan ügyletre is bukkant, amelyeknek összértéke kiemelkedő, és amelyeknél felmerül a hűtlen kezelés és a hivatali visszaélés gyanúja. A Magyar Fejlesztési Bank két körben is jegyzett le Waberer's kötvényeket, 2022-ben 111 millió euró, majd 2026-ban további 100 millió euró, vagyis összesen 77 milliárd forint értékben. A második finanszírozási kör esetében ráadásul Kapitány szerint a pénzt az MFB a saját forrásköltsége alatt biztosította, az így keletkező veszteséget pedig, a költségvetésből finanszírozott kamatkiegyenlítési rendszeren keresztül, vagyis, ahogy Kapitány István hangsúlyozta, az adófizetők pénzéből kompenzálta. A miniszter a videóban arról beszélt, hogy a két ügylet között a Waberer's tulajdonosi struktúrája jelentős átalakuláson ment át: 2022-ben megjelent a cég tulajdonosai között a Tiborcz István tulajdonában álló BDPST Group, 2023-ban tovább növelte részesedését, 2026-ban pedig, amikor a második körös finanszírozás történt, már Tiborcz István gyakorolta a végső kontrollt a vállalat felett. Kapitány szerint ez a finanszírozási konstrukció a teljes futamidő alatt akár 10 milliárd forint terhet is jelenthet a költségvetésnek, „melyet végső soron a magyar embereknek kellene megfizetnie”. A hatósági vizsgálatnak a miniszter szerint ezért arra is választ kell adnia, „hogy jogszerű volt-e egyáltalán a Waberer's vállalati kötvényfinanszírozását a központi költségvetésből finanszírozott kamatkiegyenlítési rendszerbe bevonni, és ténylegesen mekkora vagyoni hátrány érte vagy érhette az államot. Az állami vagyon nem magánvagyon, a közpénz pedig nem kiváltságok és politikailag kiváltságosok finanszírozására szolgál. A kormány feladata, hogy minden egyes forinttal elszámoljon, és ahol az állam megkárosításának gyanúja merül fel, ott megtegye a szükséges jogi lépéseket. Ezt tesszük most is” – zárta videóját a miniszter. A Waberer's alapítója és névadója, Wáberer György 2016-ban szállt ki a kamionos cégből, majd 2020-ban ismét tulajdonossá vált, hogy aztán 2023-ban a Tiborcz-féle BDPST-csoporthoz tartozó Merkport Zrt. kivásárolja Wáberer részesedéseit. Wáberer György a választások előtt kritikusan szólalt fel az Orbán-kormány és annak gazdasági rendszere kapcsán. A Telexnek a választások előtt pár nappal adott interjújában például azt mondta, árulónak tartja a Fidesz felső vezetését. Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/pari.text: Este „absurd” să se afirme că soldații francezi prezenți în Ucraina participă direct la conflict, așa cum a făcut-o ministrul rus al Afacerilor Externe, a declarat marți ministrul francez delegat pentru Apărare, Alice Rufo. Întrebată despre prezența în Ucraina a militarilor francezi pentru misiuni de instruire și întreținere, dezvăluită luni, ministra a subliniat „lipsa oricărei intenții de luptă, spre deosebire de ceea ce a afirmat, de altfel, ministrul rus al Afacerilor Externe marți dimineață, vorbind despre participarea directă la război, ceea ce este absurd”, scrie Le Figaro . „Nu mai este vorba de un sprijin acordat Ucrainei, ci de o participare directă la război”, declarase cu câteva ore înainte Serghei Lavrov în cadrul unei conferințe de presă la Manila, în Filipine, unde are loc un summit al Asociației Națiunilor din Asia de Sud-Est (ASEAN). Conform informațiilor dezvăluite luni și confirmate între timp, mici grupuri de soldați francezi se află pe teritoriul Ucrainei invadate de Rusia pentru a oferi instruire militarilor ucraineni și pentru a asigura misiuni de întreținere a anumitor echipamente furnizate de Franța, în cadrul sprijinului european acordat Kievului. „Într-adevăr, în Ucraina există o structură de coordonare care colaborează strâns cu misiunea de apărare (reprezentanța militară oficială a Franței, n.r.), ceea ce permite organizarea unor instruiri specifice în mod punctual, precum și întreținerea sau repararea echipamentelor”, a declarat Alice Rufo, răspunzând la o întrebare privind natura acestor misiuni și necesitatea sau nu de a informa Parlamentul în acest sens. Pe lângă „absența oricărei intenții de luptă”, ministra a subliniat că „numărul personalului implicat este foarte limitat”. Ea a evidențiat, de asemenea, „caracterul extrem de punctual” al misiunilor, care se desfășoară, de altfel, „la o distanță foarte mare de linia frontului”. Din aceste motive, „nu este vorba de o intervenție militară armată în cadrul unui război și de o participare directă la conflict în sensul articolului 35 din Constituție”, care reglementează controlul parlamentar asupra operațiunilor militare franceze în afara granițelor. Pe 16 noiembrie, postul de radio RFI a relatat că trupele franceze sunt staționate în secret în Ucraina cel puțin din vara anului 2026. Jurnaliștii au subliniat că francezii nu participă la operațiuni de luptă, ci doar antrenează trupele ucrainene și repară echipamente. Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News

https://avn.com/news/gay/belami-set-to-u.text: BelAmi Set to Unveil 'Rhyheim Is An American In Prague' BelAmi brings back iconic franchise with superstar Rhyheim Shabazz. To mark the occasion, BelAmi will stream the original 1997 classic, fully remastered in HD for the first time ever starting Nov. 10. SR Shane Richards By Shane Richards November 5, 2026 · 12:50 PM · 2 min read PRAGUE, CZECH REPUBLIC —BelAmi on Thursday announced the return of one of the most celebrated franchises in gay adult entertainment with Rhyheim Is An American in Prague , an ambitious new feature starring two-time GayVN Performer of the Year Rhyheim Shabazz. Filmed on location in BelAmi's scenic hometown of Prague, the anticipated feature brings a fresh face, a new adventure, and a new chapter to the franchise. Premiering Nov. 19, only at BelAmiOnline , the new production promises all the romance, adventure, steamy encounters, and the gorgeous Central European scenery that made An American in Prague a BelAmi signature. For Rhyheim, being one of the world's most sought-after gay superstars comes with its demands. Sometimes even megastars need to escape. While relaxing in Brazil and scrolling online, Rhyheim discovers 'BelAmi Tours'. Before long, he's trading the Brazilian sunshine for the enchanting fairytale streets (and boys) of Prague. Upon arrival, Rhyheim is greeted by his tour guide, BelAmi's Hugo Carter, who sets the stage for a Prague adventure. The journey takes Rhyheim through the city's enchanting streets, where unexpected encounters and a memorable succession of BelAmi's finest await. "Rhyheim shines in this project," says BelAmi's CEO Stuart. "His charisma, natural charm, and ability to perform at the highest level are truly a sight to behold. We're excited to bring this one-of-a-kind production to our members around the world. I can't think of a better way to bring back the classic An American in Prague franchise today than with Rhyheim." Released in 1997, An American in Prague is widely regarded as one of the best-selling gay adult video releases of all time and remains a defining production in BelAmi's history. The original film centers around Chance, an American visitor arriving at Prague airport, where he meets Johan Paulik. What follows is a series of interconnected encounters and city tours, with the stunning architecture and romanticism of one of Europe's most beautiful cities providing the backdrop. Alongside Johan and an iconic cast of BelAmi models, Chance discovers the magic of Prague and BelAmi. The critical and commercial success of An American in Prague would inspire multiple remakes. In 2013, BelAmi revisited the franchise with popular exclusive American model Mick Lovell, delivering another international bestseller. In 2018, BelAmi struck gold once again with Blake Mitchell Is An American in Prague, starring beloved American superstar Blake Mitchell. The multi-award-winning remake reignited worldwide enthusiasm for the series. In honor of the franchise's return with Rhyheim, BelAmi is inviting fans to rediscover where it all began. For the first time ever, the original An American in Prague will be available to stream for members of BelAmiOnline.com . Remastered in HD, the original film returns to the screen with a new level of visual clarity, allowing longtime fans and a new generation of viewers to experience the iconic movie like never before. The remastered original will roll out as a special six-part streaming event, with the first episode premiering Tuesday, Nov. 10, followed by a new episode every week for the next five weeks. It will run in conjunction with the launch of Rhyheim Is An American in Prague , creating an online event that bridges nearly three decades of BelAmi history. Bolsonaro's son Carlos wrote on X that the former far-right leader was taken to the hospital on Friday and was found to have "a near-complete intestinal obstruction." The DF Star Hospital in Brasília said that Bolsonaro was suffering from "abdominal distension" and was being examined. Bolsonaro's history of hospitalizations ​Bolsonaro, who is 71 years old, ‌has undergone several hospitalizations and surgeries since he was stabbed in the abdomen on the campaign trail for the 2018 elections. "He is being given medication for pain and an initial attempt to reverse the condition without the need for invasive intervention," Carlos said. Son blames house arrest for Bolsonaro's health issues Bolsonaro was in power from 2019 to ​2022. He was convicted last year for plotting a coup after his defeat to current President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in the 2022 election but claims being the victim of a left-wing judicial witch hunt. Bolsonaro was placed under humanitarian house arrest on medical grounds. Carlos on Friday railed against his father's detention, which he blamed for Bolsonaro's current health problems. Carlos said that the senior Bolsonaro's health was "deteriorating every day in prison due to his lack of mobility" and what he called "the psychological torture he suffers daily." Another one of Bolsonaro's sons, Flavio Bolsonaro, recently lost the October presidential election to incumbent President Lula . Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil after the vote and now resides in Florida . https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text: Decision to deny visas dismayed opposition politicians and other critics who accused government of betraying Ireland’s record of solidarity with Palestinians. Photograph: Emilija Jefremova/Reuters View image in fullscreen Decision to deny visas dismayed opposition politicians and other critics who accused government of betraying Ireland’s record of solidarity with Palestinians. Photograph: Emilija Jefremova/Reuters Ireland Twenty Gaza students due to leave for Ireland after winning visa battle Group’s evacuation follows campaign to overturn decision to deny visas to more than 60 students from territory Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent Mon 23 Nov 2026 08.03 EST Last modified on Mon 23 Nov 2026 11.09 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Twenty students from Gaza are to travel to Ireland to take up scholarships after winning a battle for visas that undercut the Irish government’s reputation as a champion of Palestinians . The group is due to leave the territory on Monday under strict Israeli controls and travel via Jordan to Dublin to take up places at Irish universities. Another group is expected to follow next month. The evacuation comes after a four-month campaign to overturn a decision by the Irish Department of Justice to deny visas to more than 60 students in Gaza who had been offered scholarships in Ireland . The decision dismayed opposition politicians and other critics who accused the department of betraying Ireland’s record of solidarity with Palestinians. The government backed down last week after a Dublin high court ordered the department to reconsider the decision. The minister for justice, Jim O’Callaghan, approved 48 visas. The first group is expected to arrive on Tuesday, with the remainder coming in late December. “It’s a mix of feelings I still can’t fully describe,” Amir Alareer, 26, who is to study cybersecurity and artificial intelligence at University College Dublin, said via email on the eve of his departure from Gaza . “There is hope and relief after months of waiting and fighting for this moment. But it is hard to feel complete joy when I am leaving my family behind in Gaza, and when 28 of my fellow students, who hold the same visas and share the same dreams, are still here waiting.” The students originally expected to come in summer, and had supporting paperwork from Irish universities, but in July the Department of Justice rejected the visa applications. “The refusals hit us hard,” said Alareer. The department demanded bank statements, proof of intention to return and other documents and said any appeal would have to be made by post, saying screening and verification were integral to the immigration system. The students said such documents had not previously been requested and that Gaza’s banking and postal service had been destroyed. Ivana Bacik, a legislator and leader of the Labour party, accused the department of using “spurious reasons” amid a hardening of immigration policy. Alareer helped to lead a campaign from Gaza that was backed in Ireland by demonstrators, a petition and an open letter signed by actors, writers and artists including Hozier, Nicola Coughlan and the rap group Kneecap. “Running a campaign from Gaza, through blackouts and displacement, was not easy, but I knew that if we stayed silent, our case would be forgotten,” said Alareer. In October, the high court ruled that there were “significant and demonstrable errors” in the refusal of a visa to Shaymaa Abudalu, a 20-year-old who had been offered an engineering scholarship at University College Cork, and who was the lead case in a batch of similar lawsuits. A high court judge welcomed the decision last week to grant 48 visas and said “huge progress” had been made. Among the students are five members of a dance troupe who have been offered places at the Irish World Academy of Music and Dance at the University of Limerick. Alareer, who studied engineering at Al-Azhar University – Gaza, said Israel ’s attacks on Gaza had destroyed his home and displaced the family several times. “The hardest experience of all was the famine, when we couldn’t find even a single kilo of flour.” Floods have impeded recent relief efforts. His family was proud of his scholarship, he said, but saying goodbye would be hard. “They are happy that I finally have this opportunity, but leaving them behind after everything we have been through together is incredibly difficult.” After studying software and innovation in Dublin, Alareer plans to return to Al-Azhar University and establish a cybersecurity department. “I want to build a generation of Palestinian engineers and researchers who can protect our digital future. Gaza will be rebuilt, and its systems must be rebuilt securely, by its own people.” Explore more on these topics Ireland Gaza Palestine Europe Middle East and north Africa news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.politico.eu/article/rachel-k.text: LONDON — The U.N. climate COP process needs urgent reform before next year’s summit in Ethiopia, the U.K.’s top climate official said. Rachel Kyte said countries must “take a red pen” to COP bureaucracy in order to save the talks. COP31 talks in Antalya, Turkey, broke down without a deal on Sunday — the first time in 17 years that countries have failed to reach consensus. Advertisement Advertisement The U.K., alongside the EU, many developing countries and small island states, rejected a draft deal that omitted any reference to fossil fuels, which fuel global warming. Kyte, the U.K.’s special representative for climate change and one of London’s key negotiators at COP, told POLITICO that, with reform, the collapse of a deal in Turkey could yet prove a “cathartic moment” for the climate talks. Kyte said many countries “want to look at” the way COP agreements are made. Final COP texts must currently be agreed by consensus among nearly 200 countries. EU climate chief Wopke Hoekstra also told the Financial Times this week that the U.N. “needs to look into” this approach. Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh, addressing the House of Commons later on Tuesday, also said the U.K. would “work to reform the COP process and uphold its integrity so it can deliver the Paris Agreement.” Kyte said it had been “a difficult political decision” to reject the deal. “But really I think it was the right year to say ‘no text.’” Catharsis For the COP process to get back on track, reform is needed before next year’s conference, Kyte said. COP32 is scheduled to start in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in November 2027. Advertisement Advertisement “If we can be our best selves, self-organized, over the next 12 months, we will look back on COP31 as being a cathartic moment of reckoning,” she said. “I’m getting incoming calls from all kinds of places, saying: ‘This is a moment, we have to seize it.’ So, on balance, it was a tough call [to reject the deal], but I think it was the right one.” Kyte also called for changes to the “extraordinarily powerful and dominant” role given in recent years to the COP host — the presidency — which she said too often “asserts its agenda” on talks. This year’s co-hosts, Turkey and Australia, placed a major emphasis on a new electrification target, against the wishes of many countries. Kyte said that, if the U.K. and other countries had compromised on the draft deal, it might have left Ethiopia with a “messy set of agreements” to start from. “Better for them that it’s now that we say, ‘Look, this process isn’t working,’” she said. Participants are seen at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey on Nov. 9, 2026. | Burak Kara/Getty Images COPs need to become leaner and more focused on core priorities of climate mitigation and finance for poorer countries to decarbonize and adapt to a warming planet, she added. Next year Summits now had a “ridiculous agenda” of items to tackle, she said, while talks could also be sidetracked by pet projects pursued by COP hosts. Advertisement Advertisement “The presidency cannot, or should not, assert its agenda substantively onto the COP, and I had some very interesting conversations with China and a number of other countries [saying]: ‘We need to look at this.’” Kyte added: “That is not unsurprising in a multilateral bureaucratic process that we would have got ourselves into this place — but now’s the time to blow the whistle, right?” She criticized a “proliferation of of procedural issues, which don’t necessarily help move the agenda forward.” Next year’s COP will come one year before the planned conclusion of the second ‘global stocktake,’ a major milestone at which countries review progress on climate goals. U.N. scientists already say the world will overshoot the most ambitious 1.5 degrees celsius warming goal set out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. “The stocktake is, unless a miracle happens, going to show that we’re not on track,” Kyte said. She said COP needed to get back on track to ensure countries could be “more urgent” in their response to its findings, particularly in supporting poorer states. She insisted, though, that, regardless of what happens at COP, market forces were now working in favor of decarbonization, with accelerated uptake of electric vehicles and renewable energy. “I think that the trend of investment in some aspects — battery storage and renewables — [is] already underway,” she said. “And that’s unstoppable at this point.” Abby Wallace contributed additional reporting .
